content_html:
Ban on payments could independent browser developers to withdraw from market

Life

Mozilla's San Francisco office. Image: IDGNS

12 August 2026

Mozilla, the developer of Firefox, has warned that it may be forced to exit the browser market if it is no longer allowed to receive payments from Google for offering its search engine.

According to Mozilla, a ban on these payments could lead the company and other independent browser developers to withdraw from the market. This would mean the disappearance of an important distributor of search services. Mozilla argues that users would thereby lose a browser that pays a great deal of attention to privacy and security, while large technology companies would in fact gain more power over the Internet.

Mozilla sets this out in an amicus curiae brief that was filed in recent days with the United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia.

The case dates back to 2020. The US Department of Justice and a group of states accused Google at the time of having violated competition law by making arrangements that made Google the default search engine in, among other things, Apple’s Safari, Mozilla’s Firefox and Android.

In 2024, after a trial, Judge Amit Mehta of the federal court in Washington ruled that Google had unlawfully maintained its monopoly in two markets: general search services and text ads linked to search queries.

In September 2025, Mehta imposed measures that, for six years, prohibit Google from entering into exclusive distribution agreements for Google Search, Chrome, Google Assistant and the Gemini app. However, the ruling does allow Google to continue paying Apple, Mozilla and other distributors of search engines.

According to Mehta, a ban on those payments would have major consequences for these companies and for the markets in which they operate.

He stated that such a ban could lead distributors to continue offering Google as the default search engine without receiving any income for it. Another possibility would be to conclude agreements with what he considers lower-quality search engines, so that they still receive payments.

US federal and state competition authorities recently asked the court of appeals to overturn the part of Mehta’s ruling that permits these payments.

Mozilla counters that Mehta’s decision on the payments is supported by the available evidence. Among other things, the company refers to its own research, which suggests that Mozilla’s revenues would fall sharply if it had to replace Google with Bing as the default search engine in Firefox.

Mozilla stresses that with its brief it is not supporting either party in the broader lawsuit. The company is therefore not taking a position on other important issues that are at stake in the appeal.

Google is expected to submit new arguments to the court of appeals next month.

content_html_zh:
支付禁令可能导致独立浏览器开发商退出市场

Life

Mozilla 旧金山办事处。 图片来源：IDGNS

2026 年 8 月 12 日

火狐浏览器开发商 Mozilla 警告称，如果不再允许谷歌为其提供搜索引擎收取费用，该公司可能会被迫退出浏览器市场。

Mozilla 表示，禁止这些付款可能会导致该公司和其他独立浏览器开发商退出市场。 这将意味着一个重要的搜索服务分销商的消失。 Mozilla 认为，用户将因此失去一个非常注重隐私和安全的浏览器，而大型科技公司实际上将获得更多的互联网权力。

Mozilla 在最近几天向美国哥伦比亚特区上诉法院提交的一份法庭之友陈述中阐述了这一点。

该案要追溯到2020年。 美国司法部和一些州指责谷歌当时违反了竞争法，因为谷歌做出的安排使谷歌成为苹果 Safari、Mozilla Firefox 和 Android 等产品的默认搜索引擎。

2024 年，华盛顿联邦法院法官阿米特·梅塔 (Amit Mehta) 经过审判后裁定，谷歌非法维持了其在两个市场的垄断地位：一般搜索服务和与搜索查询相关的文字广告。

2025 年 9 月，梅塔采取措施，在六年内禁止谷歌签订 Google 搜索、Chrome、Google Assistant 和 Gemini 应用程序的独家分销协议。 不过，该裁决确实允许谷歌继续向苹果、Mozilla 和其他搜索引擎分销商付款。

梅塔表示，禁止这些付款将对这些公司及其所在市场产生重大影响。

他表示，这样的禁令可能会导致分销商继续提供谷歌作为默认搜索引擎，而不会从中获得任何收入。 另一种可能性是与他认为质量较低的搜索引擎达成协议，以便他们仍然收到付款。

美国联邦和州竞争主管机构最近要求上诉法院推翻梅塔裁决中允许这些付款的部分。

Mozilla 反驳说，梅塔关于付款的决定是有现有证据支持的。 除此之外，该公司还提到了自己的研究，该研究表明，如果 Mozilla 不得不用 Bing 取代 Google 作为 Firefox 的默认搜索引擎，那么 Mozilla 的收入将大幅下降。

Mozilla 强调，在其简报中，它并不支持更广泛诉讼中的任何一方。 因此，该公司不对上诉中涉及的其他重要问题表明立场。

预计谷歌将于下个月向上诉法院提交新的论点。

埃默塞
